findings.summary: The batched "fast path" does NOT reproduce the registry op it claims to accelerate, and the divergence is global, not border-only. Two compounding defects: (1) torch's F.pad(mode="reflect") is scipy's mode='mirror', NOT scipy's default mode='reflect' (verified: accel gauss matches scipy mirror to 0.000000 and differs from scipy reflect by 0.134) — so the module docstring claim "Reflect padding matches scipy's default so the interiors agree" is false; (2) for the _norm-based ops (sobel_amp, laplace, gray_range_rect) the per-image max-abs normalisation divides by a GLOBAL max that frequently lands on a border pixel, so the border-convention difference rescales EVERY pixel by a constant factor (measured interior ratio 0.9659, uniform to 6 digits). findings.summary: xkor_harris declares out_sort=image (float64 in [0,1]) but returns signed values in [-1,1]: it applies _norm() WITHOUT np.abs(), unlike every sibling response op which goes through _resp() = _norm(np.abs(...)). Harris response is det - k*trace^2 and is strongly NEGATIVE on edges, so most of the signal falls outside the image contract. On a square target 22% of pixels are negative and they carry 78.9% of the total |response|; problems._as_image() clips the pipeline output to [0,1], so that 78.9% is silently destroyed — the op advertises an edge/corner detector but delivers only the corner-positive fifth of it.

In every case ops.RT[...] returns the input array unchanged, so a whole class of genome slots is a silent no-op on small tiles/patches.

findings.expected: either a meaningful result on 4x4/8x8 inputs (clamp kernel/grid to the image size) or an explicit, visible failure
